events.title: Wright Brothers' First Powered Flight
events.description: Orville and Wilbur Wright made four brief flights at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, with their Wright Flyer. The first, piloted by Orville, lasted 12 seconds and covered about 120 feet. The longest, flown by Wilbur, lasted 59 seconds and covered 852 feet.
events.significance: These flights were the first sustained, controlled, powered heavier-than-air human flights, launching the age of aviation and transforming transportation, warfare, and global connectivity.

events.title: Simón Bolívar Dies in Santa Marta
events.description: Simón Bolívar, the Venezuelan military and political leader who led the independence of several South American nations from Spanish rule, died of tuberculosis near Santa Marta, Colombia, at age 47.
events.significance: Bolívar helped liberate Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Bolivia. His dream of a unified South America collapsed as Gran Colombia dissolved, but he remains a symbol of Latin American independence.

events.title: Birth of Ludwig van Beethoven (Baptized)
events.description: Ludwig van Beethoven was baptized in Bonn on this date. His exact birth date is unknown, but it was probably December 16, 1770.
events.significance: Beethoven became one of history's most influential composers, bridging the Classical and Romantic eras and producing works such as the Ninth Symphony that continue to shape Western music.

events.title: The Simpsons Premieres as a Half-Hour Series
events.description: The Simpsons aired its first full-length episode, 'Simpsons Roasting on an Open Fire,' on the Fox network in the United States. The show had previously appeared as shorts on The Tracey Ullman Show.
events.significance: The Simpsons became the longest-running American animated series, sitcom, and scripted primetime television series, influencing satire, animation, and popular culture worldwide.

events.title: Mohamed Bouazizi Sets Himself on Fire in Tunisia
events.description: Street vendor Mohamed Bouazizi set himself on fire in Sidi Bouzid, Tunisia, protesting police harassment and corruption. His act sparked widespread protests across the country.
events.significance: His protest ignited the Tunisian Revolution and the broader Arab Spring, which toppled several governments and reshaped politics across the Middle East and North Africa.
